A CROSS-TENANT DISCLOSURE WAS LIVE ON THE RELEASE LINE ON 2026-09-22 AND IS NOW CLOSED. Recorded at the top, with its window stated, because a reader deciding release readiness needs both halves: that it existed, and that it is fixed. CLOSED BY the merge of pull request #727. What follows describes the defect as it stood before that merge. WHAT LEAKED: on a backend with `session_mode = stateless` and identity propagation configured, the FIRST identified caller's private tool catalogue was cached in the slot every caller reads and served to all of them until TTL. V AT THE THEN-CODE-TIP `50d0cdf0`: `git show 50d0cdf0:src/backend/metadata.rs` shows `get_tools_for_binding` at `:244` deriving `let key = self.pool_key_for(binding)` at `:249` and then passing `extra_headers` at `:255` UNCONDITIONALLY into `get_cached_list_on`. `pool_key_for` (`src/backend/pool.rs:213-220`) grants a private slot ONLY to `(Some(SessionMode::PerUser), Some(binding))`; a `stateless` backend -- and a `per_user` one whose caller resolved no binding -- collapses to `PoolKey::Shared`. So the caller's minted credential went upstream and the private answer it returned was written into the shared slot's cache. PROVENANCE OF THE DEFECT: it arrived with the earlier tools keying change, NOT with the branch that was under review when it was found. That was established by reading the merged base rather than the branch, after a first analysis asserted the opposite and was withdrawn. THE MERGE DECISION INVERTED, and this is the operationally important part. Pull request #727 was initially BLOCKED on the reasoning that it INTRODUCED this leak. That reasoning was half wrong -- true for resources, resource-templates and prompts, FALSE for tools, which was already disclosing on the line. Blocking the branch would not have kept the tree safe; it would have kept a live disclosure and declined its fix. The block was withdrawn and the branch merged once BOTH review seats returned SHIP on the fix delta -- kimi with no findings, grok with one HIGH gated BEFORE-DEPLOY that concerns the isolation guard rather than this fill. WHAT THE FIX DOES: `get_cached_list_for` gates the headers on the derived key -- `let fetch_headers = match identity_key { Some(_) => extra_headers, None => &[] }` -- and `identity_key` comes from the same `match` that selects the slot, so slot and headers cannot disagree. All four families route through that one fill, so the single guard closed tools as well as the three the branch was written for. BLAST RADIUS, checked independently of the fix. The defect needs a caller-specific response AND shared storage to put it in. V: `rg -n "request_with_headers\(" src/ --glob '!*tests*'` returns two production call sites passing a non-empty header slice -- the metadata fill, which caches, and `src/backend/ops.rs:341`, the live request path, which does not. `request_attempted` derives its slot the same way, so a `stateless` live call does take the shared slot with caller headers, but its response returns to the caller who asked and nothing stores it; the only per-slot state it touches is read-only (`resend_decision`, `ops.rs:166`, calls `.read()`). The disclosure was bounded to the metadata cache path. RESIDUAL, stated so this is not read as closing the conjunct: `stateless` now serves the static-credential catalogue to everyone again, which is the documented OMISSION this row already records as the unmet half of conjunct 2. The fix converted a disclosure back into that omission. It does NOT make `stateless` serve per-caller catalogues -- that needs an uncached path or a per-identity slot, both changes to `pool_key_for`, which carries a byte-for-byte single-tenant guarantee (IDP.5). TWO ITEMS CARRIED FORWARD. MIK-7543: the new `stateless` cells cover resources, templates and prompts, and the helper's `listed_for` has no `tools/list` arm, so the family that actually leaked is covered by the shared-fill argument rather than by a test. And grok's HIGH: the isolation guard admits a backend when the caller holds a minted credential, while this fill now DROPS those headers on a shared slot -- so for an isolated-OAuth `stateless` backend the guard says admit and the fetch then runs as the gateway-held account, whose catalogue lands in the slot everyone reads. That is a different leak class, gateway-account to every caller rather than caller to caller, and the guard is the half that needs to move. THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING: the branch that introduced this for three families carried a complete mutation table -- each reverted call site reddening exactly its own family -- and a reviewer's SHIP. Every cell used a `per_user` fixture, so no mutation could reach the broken arm. A mutation table proves discrimination only over the configurations its fixtures instantiate, and the stronger it looks the less anyone asks what it does not cover. 

CONJUNCT 3 IS COVERED, AND THE REASON PREVIOUSLY RECORDED FOR IT WAS WRONG. Verified 2026-09-22. The correction matters even though the conclusion does not change, because the retired reason would have sent the next reader looking for a cache that does exist. WHAT THE RECORD SAID: a correction block below, dated 2026-09-17, reads "the MCP side has no result cache to key". That is FALSE at HEAD. `crate::cache::ResponseCache` is defined at `src/cache.rs:19` and is reached from production at `src/gateway/meta_mcp/support.rs:177`, inside `response_cache_key_for` (`support.rs:168`). WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, V at source: the MCP result cache key DOES carry the caller. `ResponseCache::response_key` (`src/cache.rs:279`) composes server, tool, an argument digest, the projection suffix, the principal and a context digest; `response_cache_key_for` then appends the retry discriminator. The principal is SHA-256 HASHED rather than appended, and the code says why: "a subject is caller-supplied text, and appending it raw lets one spell another's suffix" -- the same forgery class as MIK-7408. The context digest carries the routing profile, the protocol revision and the policy epoch, and is mixed in UNCONDITIONALLY, on the stated ground that "a suffix that is empty for a default context is a dimension that is only sometimes keyed". A caller the gateway could not identify keys as `None`, and the code records the consequence rather than hiding it: two unidentified callers share an entry. CURRENT POSITION, 2026-09-22: THE IDENTITY-KEYED METADATA CACHE WAS BUILT FOR THE TOOL CATALOGUE ONLY. The design's mechanism landed and is structurally sound, but three of the four metadata families never take a caller key, so conjunct 2 is NOT met and this row is NOT gradeable. WHAT LANDED, V: the five cache fields were deleted from the backend-wide `Backend` struct and now live on the per-caller pool slot `PooledEntry` (`src/backend/pool.rs:90-103` -- tools_cache, resend_permitted, resources_cache, resource_templates_cache, prompts_cache), and `Backend` carries a comment at `src/backend/mod.rs:82-89` recording that deleting them rather than adding a keyed path beside them is what makes the compiler enumerate every reader. The fill function takes the key and selects the cache out of the slot (`get_cached_list_on`, `metadata.rs:167-179`). The structural half of T7 PASSES at HEAD: the backend-wide static-credential transport accessor has exactly ONE production caller in the tree (`src/backend/lifecycle.rs:1101`) and it is not in any metadata fill path, so a fill reaches its transport through the slot it was keyed to. WHAT DID NOT LAND, V, and this is the row: of the four `get_cached_list_on` call sites, ONE passes a caller-derived key and THREE pass the constant. `metadata.rs:251` passes `&key`, derived from the caller binding via `tools_slot` -> `pool_key_for(binding)` (`metadata.rs:32-34`). `metadata.rs:329` (resources), `metadata.rs:357` (resource templates) and `metadata.rs:390` (prompts) each pass `&PoolKey::Shared` as a literal constant and never consult a binding. `PoolKey::Shared` carries no binding by construction, in contrast to `PoolKey::PerUser { binding }`, so those three caches are filled once and answered to every caller irrespective of verified identity. CLASSIFICATION, stated precisely because it decides the grade: this is OMISSION and over-exposure, not a cross-caller leak of identity-specific data. No identity-specific prompt, resource or template ever enters those caches, so no caller receives another caller's data. That distinction does not rescue the row -- the OPERATOR RULING of 2026-09-21 already held that omission is a leak-stop and not the mode, and it was applied to exactly this shape of argument for the tool catalogue. No principled tool-versus-prompt difference has been offered: a backend is free to gate any list by identity. TEST COVERAGE, V by counting test files referencing each field: tools_cache 5, resend_permitted 1, prompts_cache 0, resources_cache 0, resource_templates_cache 0. Three of the five fields that moved have NO test asserting per-identity isolation, so even a charitable reading of the keying leaves the row without evidence for three families and without a regression guard. The file exists -- 3.5 KB at `src/gateway/meta_mcp/policy_epoch_tests.rs` -- and **no `mod policy_epoch_tests` declaration exists anywhere in `src/`** (V: `rg -n "mod policy_epoch_tests" src/` returns nothing), so it is not part of any compilation unit and has never been built or run. It would not build if it were declared: it calls `meta.policy_epoch()` as a method at `:34` and `:90`, while `policy_epoch` is a FIELD (`pub(super) policy_epoch: Arc<AtomicU64>`, `mod.rs:579`). WHAT THE WITHDRAWAL DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE. The MECHANISM claim still stands on its own evidence: `set_identity_grants` (`mod.rs:1300`) does take the write lock, replace the store, and advance `policy_epoch` with `Release` ordering while still holding it, and that is readable at source. What is gone is the claim that any TEST pins that behaviour. The result axis of this criterion is therefore asserted by code reading alone, with no executable guard, and a future edit that reorders the bump below the lock release would be caught by nothing. WHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE, recorded because the search that would have caught it is not the obvious one. An orphaned Rust test file is invisible to BOTH of the checks a reader reaches for: coverage cannot report it, because it is not compiled; and grepping for the module name finds only the citations, because a file does not contain its own `mod` declaration -- that lives in the parent. The only check that finds it is asking whether the PARENT declares the child. Cross-check any `foo_tests.rs` cited as evidence with `rg "mod foo_tests"` before relying on it. PROPAGATION, stated so the correction reaches the same places the error did. This citation was repeated into Linear MIK-7530, into briefs given to three separate implementation agents, and into `docs/internal/design/2026-09-22-live-identity-grant-reload.md`, which cites it twice. It was found by the agent writing the criterion's failing tests -- that is, by trying to USE the evidence rather than by re-reading it, which is the only method that distinguishes a test that passes from a test that does not exist. THE BLAST RADIUS IS BOUNDED, AND THE SWEEP THAT BOUNDS IT ALMOST LIED. Every `*_tests.rs` under `src/` was checked for a declaration anywhere in the tree: **113 files, exactly ONE declared nowhere** -- this file. So this is an isolated orphan rather than a systemic gap, and the other 112 are wired. Recorded because a first pass at that sweep reported **72 orphans** and was wrong: it looked only in each file's own directory (`mod.rs` / `parent.rs`), while Rust lets a sibling declare a test module via `#[path = "..."] mod foo_tests;`, which is the common pattern here. A directory-scoped negative is not a tree-scoped verdict, and the wrong version of this check would have turned one real defect into seventy-two fictional ones. The correct check searches every `.rs` in the tree for both `mod <stem>` and a `path = "...<file>"` attribute. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S REMAINING WORK: wiring and repairing that file is now part of the revocation conjunct's implementation rather than a tidy-up. It must be declared, corrected to read the field, and RUN -- and if it fails once wired, that failure is a finding about the mechanism, not about the test.

CHANGES CONJUNCT RE-GRADED 2026-09-22: MET ON ONE PATH ONLY, NOT MET ON THE SHIPPED DEFAULT. The conjunct audit recorded CHANGES as MET on the construct from #672 -- a per-user slot served from cache only while fresh, falling through to a credentialed refetch once aged out. That is a TIME-based staleness mechanism. It self-corrects eventually; it does not isolate at the moment the authorization context changes, which is what the clause asks for. The question the audit did not put is what the per-user slot is KEYED on, and the answer differs by propagation strategy because TWO functions named cache_binding exist and either may produce PropagatedCredential::cache_binding, which is what PoolKey::PerUser { binding } carries (pool.rs:42-44). PATH A, NOT MET -- identity_propagation::cache_binding(subject_key, audience) at identity_propagation/mod.rs:316 takes no grant input at all, and subject_key is stable_actor_id(), which is format!("oidc:{issuer}:{subject}") at key_server/oidc.rs:132-140 and therefore STABLE ACROSS A GRANT ROTATION BY DESIGN. Produced at identity_propagation/mod.rs:460. PropagationError gained one variant plus non_exhaustive; 4.0.0 is unpublished (crates.io max_version is 3.5.1) so the addition is ordinary major-version work, and a major bump is the only moment non_exhaustive is free -- it is breaking in any later minor, and every future variant is non-breaking now.

UPGRADED FROM CANDIDATE TO A PROVEN MECHANISM, same day, by reading the admission body rather than rebuilding. The magnitude is still unmeasured and this row still does not claim the fix closes the criterion -- but the wasted work is now identified at file and line rather than suspected. WHAT HAPPENS ON EVERY tools/call THAT CARRIES NO IDEMPOTENCY KEY. `admit_sync` (`admission.rs:105`) opens by building `let operation = json!({"kind": "backend", "server": server, "tool": tool, "arguments": arguments, "retry": retry.key_discriminator()})` at `:117` -- a fresh `serde_json::Value` that DEEP-COPIES the whole `arguments` payload, since the parameter is `arguments: &Value` (`:113`). It then hands that to `admit_operation` (`:134`). Thirty-six lines later, at `:151`, the first thing `admit_operation` does after the malformed-retry check is `let Some(key) = retry.idempotency_key.as_deref() else { return ... Ok(SyncAdmission::Unprotected) }` (`:153`). On that arm NEITHER `operation` NOR `representation` is read. Both were constructed for nothing. THAT ARM IS EXACTLY THE ARM THE BENCHMARK TAKES, by the configuration's own account: the workload client is unauthenticated on purpose and supplies no key, and `gateway.workload.yaml` states that the legacy cells `take the same Unprotected admission arm C takes via !is_modern`. The k6 script drives `tools/call` against `gateway_invoke`, so the `admit_meta_sync` path (`:217`) runs first and evaluates `self.meta_representation(tool_name, full, session)` as a call ARGUMENT -- Rust evaluates arguments eagerly, so that value is also built and also discarded. WHY THIS MATCHES THE MEASURED SHAPE ON BOTH TERMS, which is what makes it more than a plausible story. The measurement is a raised floor of about +23 to +31 microseconds PLUS a proportional term of roughly 5 to 10 percent. Allocating the JSON map, its static keys and `key_discriminator()` is a constant per call -- that is the floor. Deep-copying `arguments` costs in proportion to the payload -- that is the proportional term. A single defect accounting for both components is a better fit than two unrelated causes, and neither baseline pays either cost because the module does not exist there. THE FIX IS DEFERRAL, NOT REMOVAL. Nothing here is wrong when a key IS supplied; the values are needed then. What is wrong is computing them before the branch that decides whether they are needed. Moving the key-presence check ahead of the construction -- or passing thunks and forcing them after it -- preserves behaviour exactly on both arms. STILL REQUIRED BEFORE THIS ROW MOVES: the paired A-versus-C re-run. A mechanism that explains the shape is not a measured improvement, and this criterion grades on the measurement.
